articles.summary: ZeroID is an open-source identity and credentialing platform designed to solve the attribution problem in autonomous and multi-agent systems by providing traceability for agent actions. articles.summary: The UK government is threatening tech executives with imprisonment if they fail to implement measures to stop the proliferation of non-consensual AI-generated nudification tools. articles.summary: The North Korean Lazarus group is leveraging legitimate US-based LLCs and GitHub typo-squatting to distribute malware through the GraphAlgo campaign, specifically targeting software developers. articles.summary: The rise of AI-powered browser extensions presents an overlooked security vulnerability, as these tools often operate without sufficient oversight or enterprise protection. articles.summary: As enterprise identity systems mature, CISOs face a growing paradox where fragmented application environments leave significant security gaps vulnerable to AI-driven threats. Research highlights that hundreds of disconnected enterprise applications create 'dark' identity risks that require immediate strategic remediation.

articles.title: AI Agents and Non-Human Identities Creating Critical Security Gaps, Report
articles.summary: A new report from Keeper Security highlights that non-human identities and automated system interactions are emerging as the primary cybersecurity risk for organizations by 2026. These gaps present significant challenges in securing machine-to-machine communications and identity management.

articles.title: AI-enabled device code phishing campaign exploits OAuth flow for account takeover
articles.summary: Microsoft researchers identified a large-scale phishing campaign that automates the exploitation of the OAuth Device Code flow to bypass security controls and compromise organizational accounts. The attackers utilize AI-assisted infrastructure to generate dynamic codes and circumvent typical authentication expiration windows.

articles.title: GitHub Copilot CLI gets a second-opinion feature built on cross-model review
articles.summary: GitHub has introduced a 'Rubber Duck' feature for its Copilot CLI that employs cross-model reviews to mitigate the risks of AI-generated coding errors. By using a second model to verify the output of the first, the tool aims to overcome the inherent blind spots found in self-reflection techniques.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds a flaw in Fortinet FortiClient EMS to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added the critical Fortinet FortiClient EMS vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-35616, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports of active exploitation. The flaw carries a CVSS score of 9.1, prompting urgent patching requirements for federal agencies.

articles.title: Comp AI: The open-source way to get compliant with SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA and GDPR
articles.summary: Comp AI is an open-source compliance platform designed to automate evidence collection and policy management for standards like SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and GDPR. By offering a self-hosted, inspectable codebase, it aims to streamline the traditional manual audit process for startups.

articles.title: OpenAI opens applications for an external AI safety research fellowship
articles.summary: OpenAI has launched a paid external fellowship program to fund research into AI safety, alignment, and robust mitigation strategies for advanced systems. The initiative seeks to engage researchers and engineers outside of the organization to address critical AI security and ethical challenges.

articles.title: New GPUBreach Attack Enables Full CPU Privilege Escalation via GDDR6 Bit-Flips
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered new RowHammer-based side-channel attacks, collectively named GPUBreach, that exploit GDDR6 memory to achieve privilege escalation and potential host control. These vulnerabilities demonstrate the first successful attempt to leverage GPU memory bit-flips for full system compromise.

articles.title: Experts published unpatched Windows zero-day BlueHammer
articles.summary: A researcher has publicly disclosed an unpatched privilege escalation zero-day vulnerability in Windows dubbed 'BlueHammer', which allows attackers to gain SYSTEM-level administrative rights. Microsoft has not yet released a patch for this flaw.

articles.title: China-Linked Storm-1175 Exploits Zero-Days to Rapidly Deploy Medusa Ransomware
articles.summary: The China-linked threat actor Storm-1175 is actively weaponizing a combination of zero-day and N-day vulnerabilities to conduct high-speed attacks and deploy Medusa ransomware. The group is noted for its high operational tempo and expert reconnaissance of exposed internet-facing assets.

articles.title: Flowise AI Agent Builder Under Active CVSS 10.0 RCE Exploitation; 12,000+ Instances Exposed
articles.summary: An open-source AI platform called Flowise is facing active exploitation of a critical CVSS 10.0 remote code execution vulnerability, putting over 12,000 instances at risk. The flaw, identified as CVE-2025-59528, allows attackers to perform arbitrary code execution via the CustomMCP node.

articles.title: The case for fixing CWE weakness patterns instead of patching one bug at a time
articles.summary: MITRE's Alec Summers advocates for addressing systemic CWE weakness patterns rather than relying on reactive, individual bug patching to improve long-term software security. The shift toward mapping CVEs to specific CWEs enhances root-cause analysis, though it requires high-quality data to ensure automation tools remain effective.

articles.title: How Mimecast brings enterprise-grade email protection to API deployment
articles.summary: Mimecast explains how its API-based email security platform helps organizations address vulnerabilities in native Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace defenses, particularly against AI-driven phishing and business email compromise.

articles.title: Google study finds LLMs are embedded at every stage of abuse detection
articles.summary: Google researchers have mapped the integration of large language models across the entire abuse detection lifecycle, highlighting a shift from traditional fine-tuned models to LLM-driven content moderation.

articles.title: Yahoo! Japan’s owner consolidating 164 OpenStack clusters into one
articles.summary: LY Corp, the owner of Yahoo! Japan, is consolidating 164 disparate OpenStack clusters into a single unified architecture to streamline cloud infrastructure management. This initiative aims to improve operational efficiency and reduce the complexity of their internal cloud environment.

articles.title: German authorities identify REvil and GangCrab ransomware bosses
articles.summary: German federal police have identified two Russian nationals as the primary leaders behind the REvil and GandCrab ransomware operations active between 2019 and 2021.

articles.title: AI agents found vulns in this popular Linux and Unix print server
articles.summary: AI agents were utilized to successfully identify security vulnerabilities within a widely used Linux and Unix print server software. This development highlights the growing role of automated AI tools in both discovering and potentially exploiting system weaknesses.

articles.title: Understanding Current Threats to Kubernetes Environments
articles.summary: Unit 42 reports an increase in Kubernetes-focused attacks where threat actors leverage identity abuse and critical vulnerabilities to compromise cloud environments. The analysis highlights the evolving tactics used by adversaries to gain unauthorized access to containerized infrastructure.

articles.title: New GPUBreach attack enables system takeover via GPU rowhammer
articles.summary: The GPUBreach attack exploits Rowhammer vulnerabilities in GDDR6 memory to perform bit-flips, enabling attackers to escalate privileges and gain full control over a system. This technique highlights a significant hardware-level security risk involving GPU memory management.

articles.title: Fortinet customers confront actively exploited zero-day, with a full patch still pending
articles.summary: Fortinet customers are facing active exploitation of two critical vulnerabilities in FortiClient EMS. While a full patch is pending, security experts are urging users to apply an immediate hotfix to mitigate risk.

articles.title: FBI: Cyber fraud surges to $17.6 billion in losses as scams, crypto theft soar
articles.summary: FBI reports indicate that cyber-enabled fraud losses reached $17.6 billion in 2025, driven significantly by an increase in scams and cryptocurrency-related theft. These fraudulent activities accounted for nearly half of all complaints received by the IC3.

articles.title: Medusa ransomware group using zero-days to launch attacks within 24 hours of breach, Microsoft says
articles.summary: The Medusa ransomware group is rapidly executing full-scale attacks, moving from initial compromise to data exfiltration and encryption in under 24 hours. Microsoft warns that the group is effectively leveraging zero-day vulnerabilities to expedite these intrusions.

articles.title: Phishing LNK files and GitHub C2 power new DPRK cyber attacks
articles.summary: North Korean threat actors are targeting South Korean organizations by using phishing emails containing malicious LNK files that deploy decoy PDFs and PowerShell scripts, utilizing GitHub as a command-and-control infrastructure.

articles.title: Big tech vows to continue CSAM scanning in Europe despite expiration of law allowing it
articles.summary: Major technology companies have committed to voluntarily continuing CSAM scanning on their platforms in Europe, despite the expiration of the legal framework that previously mandated these efforts.

articles.title: Disgruntled researcher leaks “BlueHammer” Windows zero-day exploit
articles.summary: A disgruntled security researcher publicly disclosed a zero-day privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows, known as BlueHammer, which allows attackers to gain SYSTEM-level access. The exploit remains unpatched by Microsoft.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes Classic Outlook bug causing email delivery issues
articles.summary: Microsoft has patched a technical bug in the Classic version of Outlook that was preventing users from successfully sending emails via Outlook.com. The resolution addresses a functional service disruption rather than a security exploit.

articles.title: Iran-Linked Password-Spraying Campaign Targets 300+ Israeli Microsoft 365 Organizations
articles.summary: An Iran-linked threat actor is conducting a multi-wave password-spraying campaign targeting over 300 Microsoft 365 organizations in Israel and the U.A.E. amidst regional conflict.
